title: Secrets provenance and attested rotation notes (v0.1, draft)
content:
Summary:
This note collects a pragmatic approach for adding secrets provenance and attested key-rotation to on-prem/VPC private deployments. The goal is to reduce blast radius from compromised nodes, provide verifiable rotation events (signed provenance), and make Terraform-driven upgrades repeatable and auditable. This is intentionally prescriptive but still a draft — focus is on an operationally testable migration path that meshes HSM-backed root keys, short-lived KMS wrapping keys, and SIEM-friendly audit export.

Motivation & goals:
- Ensure every secrets rotation event is tied to an attestation (machine/identity) and a key-ceremony signature so customers and auditors can trace who/what requested rotation.
- Replace long-lived static encryption keys used by secrets-backplane with ephemeral wrapping keys issued by an internal KMS or HSM gateway.
- Make Terraform changes idempotent and safe for rolling upgrades in customer air-gapped environments.
- Produce tamper-evident audit streams to both local audit-store and optional cloud SIEM (via egress gateway).

Assumptions:
- Customers may have an HSM (PKCS#11) or a cloud KMS reachable via a private endpoint.
- There is a secrets-backplane (existing) that currently stores encrypted blobs using a single cluster-wide AES key.
- We can deploy lightweight attestation agents on nodes (TPM / attestation-server) and run a key ceremony with operator involvement.

High-level design:
1) Root-of-trust remains HSM or external KMS: generate a 4096-bit RSA or EC key pair used only for signing provenance metadata. Private material stays in HSM; only signing operations allowed.
2) Introduce ephemeral wrapping keys (30d default TTL) provisioned by a local KMS gateway. Wrapping keys encrypt AES DEK used by secrets-backplane.
3) Each rotation event yields three artifacts: rotation-record.json (signed by HSM root key), signed-attestation.jwt (node identity & firmware hash), and terraform-plan-change metadata. These three together provide provenance.
4) Audit export pipeline: rotation events are appended to local append-only audit log (immutable WAL) and forwarded, in masked form, to SIEM via the egress-proxy with enforced mTLS.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- New module: modules/attested-kms-gateway: handles PKCS#11 connector config, KMS GRPC endpoint, and CA cert bootstrap. Keep interface minimal: input HSM connection string, attestation-policy-id, allowed-principal-list.
- Add resource: redwood_hsm_key_signer (internal provider) that wraps HSM signing calls. This is a thin provider shim (see PR #822).
- Migration plan in TF: two-phase apply. Phase A (canary): deploy gateway in canary namespace with read-only hook and sign-only capability; Phase B: cutover secrets-backplane to use wrapper keys via config flag.
- Terraform state considerations: do not store plaintext key material in state; store key references (URIs) and rotation tokens only. Use remote state locked by SRE with restricted access.

Attested rotation workflow (operator flow):
1) Operator triggers rotation via CLI (redwood-ctl rotate-secret --path /services/xyz).
2) Node agent collects measurements (TPM quote / firmware hash), operator supplies human confirmation code.
3) Gateway requests a new wrapping key from KMS/HSM (30d TTL), performs an envelope encrypt of DEK, signs rotation-record with HSM root key.
4) Secrets-backplane receives new wrapped DEK and performs an atomic swap with old DEK, streaming re-encryption of hot cache where feasible.
5) Rotation artifacts written to local audit WAL and forwarded to SIEM.

Upgrade/migration plan (steps + guardrails):
- Phase 0: prepare testbed and dry-run. Create simulated HSM (SoftHSM) and a staging KMS gateway.
- Phase 1: deploy attestation-agent and gateway in canary cluster (1 node). Run scripted rotations, verify signed records and validation flows.
- Phase 2: enable read-only verification in production path (no swap). Monitor for verification errors for 24–72h.
- Phase 3: gradual rollout (10%→25%→50%→100%) with automatic rollback on verification failures >0.5% over 1h window.
- Phase 4: deprecate old AES master key after grace period and final audit.

Testing and validation:
- Automated tests: unit signer tests, e2e rotation harness that validates signature chain, attestation token verification, and audit log tamper detection.
- Chaos tests: simulate node compromise where attestation fails; ensure rotation is rejected and alerts generated.
- Pen-testing: include red-team scenarios for HSM interface, egress-proxy, and terraform state leakage.

Audit log schema (minimum fields):
- event_id, timestamp, subject (operator/principal), target_secret_path, old_key_ref, new_key_ref, attestation_jwt_ref, rotation_signature_ref, terraform_plan_id, severity

Operational notes & corner cases:
- Air-gapped installs: provide offline key ceremony tool that exports signed rotation-records as USB-signed bundles. Bundle verification must be deterministic.
- Rollback: if swap fails, system should fallback to previous DEK and quarantine the partially-updated nodes. Documented CLI commands for rollback are essential.
- Compromised HSM key: plan requires pre-provisioned secondary HSM root key in escrow with multi-party access (3-of-5 quorum). Key revocation path must invalidate all derived wrapping keys.

Open questions:
- TTL defaults when customer policies mandate shorter rotations (7d). Can we support sub-24h rotation safely with current re-encryption windows?
- How to present provenance UI in Console without leaking sensitive metadata (secret paths)? Consider hashed path+salt view.
- Should Terraform provider surface attestation-policy evaluation results in plan output or only in apply-time logs?

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: prototype modules/attested-kms-gateway + internal provider shim (due 2024-11-20).
- Marcus: implement audit WAL and SIEM forwarder in staging (due 2024-11-28).
- Elena: write attestation-agent hardening checklist and offline ceremony guide (due 2024-12-05).

References and links:
- GH PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/822
- Related Confluence: PRIV-SEC-PROV-1 (attestation design)
- JIRA epic: PRIVSEC-891

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive. Aim for a hands-on validation in the next two sprints; feedback on Terraform interfaces and rollback semantics is most valuable.
